portal.title: CC6
portal.intro: Every subject in one place — what there is to learn, and how far you have come.

subjects.title: Math
subjects.desc: Number sense, operations, geometry and data

items.title: Place value
items.desc: The value of a digit depends on its position: ones, tens, hundreds, tenths, hundredths.

items.title: Comparing and ordering numbers
items.desc: Use place value and number lines to compare whole numbers and decimals.

items.title: Meaning of a fraction
items.desc: A fraction names equal parts of a whole or a set: numerator over denominator.

items.title: Equivalent fractions
items.desc: Different fractions that name the same amount, such as 1/2 = 2/4 = 3/6.

items.title: Adding and subtracting fractions
items.desc: With like denominators add the numerators; with unlike denominators find a common one first.

items.title: Multiplication strategies
items.desc: Arrays, area models, partial products and the standard algorithm.

items.title: Division and remainders
items.desc: Equal sharing and equal grouping; interpreting what a remainder means.

items.title: Order of operations
items.desc: Parentheses, then multiplication and division, then addition and subtraction, left to right.

items.title: Perimeter and area
items.desc: Perimeter is the distance around a shape; area is the space it covers, in square units.

items.title: Angles
items.desc: Acute, right, obtuse and straight angles, measured in degrees with a protractor.

items.title: Classifying 2-D shapes
items.desc: Sort polygons by sides, angles, parallel and perpendicular lines.

items.title: Bar graphs and dot plots
items.desc: Organise data and read it to answer questions.

items.title: Mean, median and mode
items.desc: Three ways to describe the centre of a data set.

items.title: Phonemic awareness
items.desc: Hearing and working with the individual sounds in spoken words.

items.title: Phonics and decoding
items.desc: Connecting letters and letter patterns to sounds to read words.

items.title: Reading fluency
items.desc: Reading with accuracy, a good rate and expression.

items.title: Main idea and details
items.desc: What a text is mostly about, and the details that support it.

items.title: Making inferences
items.desc: Using clues in the text plus what you know to reach a conclusion.

items.title: Text structure
items.desc: Sequence, compare and contrast, cause and effect, problem and solution.

items.title: Story elements
items.desc: Characters, setting, plot, conflict and resolution.

items.title: The writing process
items.desc: Plan, draft, revise, edit and publish.

items.title: Opinion and argument writing
items.desc: State a claim and support it with reasons and evidence.

items.title: Parts of speech
items.desc: Nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, pronouns and more.

items.title: Prefixes and suffixes
items.desc: Word parts that change a word's meaning, such as un-, re-, -ful, -less.

subjects.title: Science
subjects.desc: Matter, forces, Earth and living things

items.title: States of matter
items.desc: Solids, liquids and gases, and how heating and cooling change them.

items.title: Mixtures and solutions
items.desc: Substances combined without a chemical change; some can be separated.

items.title: Forces and motion
items.desc: Pushes and pulls change an object's speed or direction.

items.title: Forms of energy
items.desc: Light, heat, sound, electrical and mechanical energy.

items.title: The water cycle
items.desc: Evaporation, condensation, precipitation and collection.

items.title: Weathering and erosion
items.desc: Wind, water and ice break down rock and move it.

items.title: Sun, Earth and Moon
items.desc: Rotation causes day and night; revolution causes the year; the Moon's phases.

items.title: Food chains and webs
items.desc: How energy moves from producers to consumers and decomposers.

items.title: Adaptations
items.desc: Body parts and behaviours that help living things survive.

items.title: Life cycles
items.desc: The stages of life of plants and animals, such as metamorphosis.

items.title: The thirteen colonies
items.desc: New England, Middle and Southern colonies, each shaped by geography and economy.

items.title: The American Revolution
items.desc: From taxation without representation to independence in 1776 and victory in 1781.

items.title: The Constitution
items.desc: Written in 1787; the Bill of Rights followed in 1791.

items.title: Texas history
items.desc: Native peoples, Spanish missions, the Texas Revolution and statehood.

items.title: Map skills
items.desc: Compass rose, scale, legend, latitude and longitude.

items.title: Regions of Texas
items.desc: Coastal Plains, North Central Plains, Great Plains, Mountains and Basins.

items.title: Three branches of government
items.desc: Legislative makes laws, executive enforces them, judicial interprets them.

items.title: Rights and responsibilities
items.desc: Freedoms citizens have and duties such as voting and obeying laws.

items.title: Supply and demand
items.desc: How the amount available and how much people want it affect price.

items.title: Needs, wants and scarcity
items.desc: Limited resources mean making choices.
